say: Green fields, clean roads, a paladin every mile. Nobody look like a thief.
Holy country. Knives out of sight, mouths shut.
River raptors in the fields and priests on the road.
Everything here's tidy. Tidy places have good cells.
Keep your spacing.
Agreed. Eyes open.
Same here. Stay sharp.
Then we move faster.
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: Please don't say things like that.
I was hoping you'd say it was nothing.
Can we go around? Please?
Why must you say it out loud?
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: Cheer up. Might be nicer than it looks.
Could be worse. Probably.
Worry later, when it bites.
You worry too much. Keep walking.
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: Then we face it. Walk on.
Fear is for the weak. Walk.
A warrior walks into it. So shall we.
Don't slow. Don't flinch.
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: We heard it too. Stay close.
We're listening as well.
Yes. We noticed. Walk.
We'll keep near the others.
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: Acknowledged.
Noted. Continuing.
Observation logged.
Understood. Advancing.
then.speaker: T_INTERJECTOR1

say: Patrols on every hill. Stay on the road, nod, pay nothing.
Richest ground on the map and they guard it like a vault.
Anyone carrying a stolen blade should lose it now.
A hundred paladins within a day's walk. I count them on every road.
It's lovely. Why does it feel like being watched by a schoolmaster?
Everyone is so clean. I feel like mud.
Please don't say anything about the Flame.
They look at us as if they're deciding what we are.
Fertile soil, polite bigots. Smile and keep walking.
Pretty place to be hated in.
Look at all that farmland. Someone ought to rob it, and it won't be me.
Nice weather. Shame about the neighbours.
Flatskin priests and flatskin farms. Rich ground, rotten hands.
The Holy Nation grew fat on green land. The Kingdom grew strong on sand.
I won't bow here. I won't fight either, unless I must.
They look at me as a beast. Let them.
Eyes on us. We feel them like hands.
We were never welcome in this country.
The grass is soft here. The people aren't.
Stay close, all of us. We've done this before.
Holy Nation territory. Hostile intent probable.
They call us abominations here. Reminder logged.
Population dense. Evasion difficult.
Be advised that I'm the least welcome of us.
Two mountains and a lot of holy army between them.
Half grass, half desert, all patrols. Pick which half you die in.
Paladins keep these roads. Roads are for people who pay for them.
I had a cousin conscripted up here. Never saw him again, which was a mercy.
The valley funnels everything onto the roads. That's how they like it.
Outlaws in the hills, holy army on the road.
If a patrol stops us, we're pilgrims.
Good ground for an ambush and I'd rather it were somebody else's.
The mountains are beautiful. I wish they weren't so close on both sides.
Are those soldiers? They're soldiers. They're looking at us.
Please let us not be stopped. Please let us not be stopped.
I used to want to see the Holy Nation. I can stop wanting now.
A valley full of zealots. Lovely scenery.
Keep your head down and your cloak up. I hate this road already.
Someone is always praying, somewhere. It gets into the water.
Grass on one side, sand on the other. Neat, like it was ordered.
Holy soldiers look at me like a thing they would like to bring to heel.
This valley belongs to those who would break us.
The flatskins here pray for our deaths. We can answer in kind.
If they come, I'll be the first to meet them. Don't hold me back.
The valley is a mouth. We're walking down it.
Soldiers on the ridge. They have not decided about us yet.
We don't belong here. We won't stay long.
Humans fear what they can't sing to.
Valley walls limit escape routes. Advise caution.
Holy army presence high. My presence is a violation of their law.
Elevation advantage lies with the ridges.
I'll walk at the rear. They'll see me last.
Flat, dry, open. You can see trouble coming and still not outrun it.
West edge of Holy country. Where they send the ones they're sick of.
Stack is somewhere ahead. Holy walls, holy cells, holy sermons about both.
Fog on the sea side. I hope it stays there.
Open ground. Patrols can see us from a long way off.
Seta's people watch this border. Shek come up from the south, so they watch everyone.
The Fog Islands lie off the coast. Don't camp on the shore.
Quiet. That's the part I don't like.
It's so flat. Nowhere to hide.
Is that fog out there? On the water? Does it move?
I don't want to meet an inquisitor. Do they come out here?
I keep waiting for something to jump out of all this nothing.
The edge of everything holy and the beginning of everything weird.
The sea's out there somewhere. I can smell it, and something worse.
Gulf, they call it. Looks like a long walk to me.
Edge of the map's good side. Keep sipping, we'll need it.
The Holy Nation's western edge. We've fought them from the south. I wonder how they hold here.
Stack is near. A flatskin fort for flatskin priests.
The sea air is wet. I don't like it.
Seta watches this border, so they say.
We're near the fog. Something in it calls, and not in a kind voice.
The land is wide here. Wide enough to be seen from far away.
Something walks at the edge of the mist. We keep our eyes forward.
The sea speaks softly. Under the sea speaks something else.
Coastal terrain. Salt corrosion probable.
Holy border presence detected. Maintaining distance.
Fog formations visible to the west.
Low cover. Wide sight lines. Neither favours us.
Mountains on both sides and a holy fort on one of them.
Heard the machinists are somewhere up the west side. Smart folk.
Hard walking and nothing to steal.
If the paladins see us, we are lost pilgrims. Look lost.
Military hardpoints on the east arm. Don't wander up there to look.
The west side is Tech Hunter ground. They sell, they don't give.
Narrow paths. Walk in file and keep your hands off the rocks.
A rockfall here would end us. I don't like the sound of this slope.
It's so steep. My legs are shaking.
Are there people up there? Real people? Or just soldiers?
I want to sit down. I want to sit down somewhere with a wall.
Every shadow on that ridge is a paladin. Every one.
Good air. Terrible company, if we meet any.
Mountains are fine. The people living in them are the problem.
My knees hate this. My knees speak for all of us.
Higher ground is nice. Until someone higher is holding a crossbow.
Mountain ground favours the one who holds the top. Let us hold it.
The Holy Nation puts forts in the hills. We would have put a hammer there.
I climb slowly, not weakly. Wait for me.
These cliffs have seen enough battles. Add no more unless we must.
The stone is cold. We like the cold, it doesn't argue.
High places let the wind carry. We hear everything from here.
Soldiers above. Machinists below. We belong to neither.
We walk the rock together. If one slips, we all stop.
Mountain terrain. Footing hazardous.
Eastern slope contains military installations. Avoid.
Tech Hunter presence on western slope.
I don't tire. This isn't an achievement. This is a design.
Border Zone. Dust Bandits, Starvers, ninjas, and Shek, all hating each other.
Plenty of ore here, plenty of knives. Dig carefully, if you dig.
The Hub is somewhere out there, all ruins now. Plenty to scrape.
Everybody's first stop and half of them never get a second.
No patrols to speak of. That's why the bandits breed here.
Tech Hunters, dust, and old Holy ruins.
Squin keeps the Shek side. Use it as a landmark and as an exit.
Watch the horizons. Starvers come in packs, Dust Bandits come in hundreds.
I remember this. This is where I started. Please don't remind me.
Bandits on both sides, they say. Which side is this?
Everything is brown and nothing is safe.
I have a little money. I'd like to keep it. Can we run fast?
The crossroads of bad ideas. We fit right in.
Rich ore, rich bandits. Everyone's got something worth stealing.
Home sweet nothing. I'll drink to it.
There's an honest living in these rocks, and I mean to find it before the thieves do.
The ground between Kingdom and Holy Nation.
Squin holds the line. Lesser men hold the dust.
Bandits here wear the dirt as honour. They will find none.
A good place to train. Bring your spear and your patience.
Many hungry people live here. We understand hunger.
The dust carries voices. Not all of them sound friendly.
We have no quarrel with the bandits. They have one with us.
Tech Hunters and traders pass. We could trade, if we were allowed.
Border Zone. Multiple hostile factions. Probable contact.
Rich in ore. Poor in security.
The Hub is a ruin. The Holy Nation lost it.
Starving bandits don't discriminate. I find that fair.
Shek country. Everyone here's seven feet of grudge. Nobody stare.
Kral's Chosen come out of these dunes. Don't say that name loud.
Sand, spiders, and warriors with something to prove. Pick a fight with none.
The heat doesn't kill you. The Shek do, if you're rude.
Shek honour is a clock. Don't be the thing that makes it strike.
Skin spiders have drifted in from the west. They don't care about honour.
Berserkers and Kral's Chosen. Both will kill you for a reason.
Water first. Rest second. Talk third. This isn't a hospitable place.
It's so hot. I could faint right here.
Are Shek always so tall? Are they always so serious?
Please don't insult anybody. Please don't even look at anybody.
Everything here wants to be left alone and will kill you for it.
Sunburn and sword-play. A fine way to meet new people.
Pretty, in a deadly way. Walk soft, drink often.
I like the quiet. I like the quiet less with spiders in it.
Be kind to everyone you meet. They'll be seven feet tall.
The desert is my mother. Her breath is hot. I'm glad of it.
Home. Even this far, the sand knows my name.
The Stone Golem hears us, always.
We aren't many, and we aren't weak.
The sun is bright. The Shek are bright.
We walk in the shadow of those who don't hate us.
Dry. We prefer the Hive's warm dark.
The spiders aren't our kin. Don't call them that.
High heat. Sand ingress. Maintenance required.
Shek territory. Relations are tolerable. Maintain courtesy.
Skin spiders. Motion detected. Weapons ready.
The dunes shift. The map does not. Recalibrating.
Hills full of spiders. I could do with a fire and a hundred miles.
Skin spiders. They go for the neck. Keep your collars up.
Ain't nothing here but bugs and bones. And we're about to add to the pile.
Stay on high ground. The things like to come at you from the low.
Skin spiders in packs. Back to back if they come.
Old Shek ground that the Shek gave up. That tells me what I need to know.
Spiders at dusk are worse. Move while there's light.
Don't stand in the tall grass. Anything can wait in the tall grass.
I hate spiders. I hate them so much. I hate this place.
Is that webbing? That looks like webbing.
I felt something crawl on my neck. Tell me I imagined it.
I'd rather the bandits, honestly. Bandits you can talk to.
Never met a spider I liked. This is a whole field of them.
I wonder how many hundred legs are watching us.
Keep walking. And whatever you do, don't look up.
Pretty hills. Terrible tenants.
Once this land was ours. Spiders hold it now.
I have killed spiders larger than this.
The Kingdom's hold here has faded. We should remember how to hold.
Nothing here stands against a Shek spear.
The crawling things feel us. They don't like our song.
We aren't the only ones who walk in numbers.
Spiders hunt by shaking the earth. Walk softly, all of us.
We watch for them. We always watch.
Skin spider habitat. Probability of contact high.
Metal doesn't interest them. Flesh does.
Hostile arthropods detected. Advise formation.
I'll lead through the grass. I have less to lose.
Ring of mountains round a place you don't come back from. We're only walking the ring.
Bounty hunters and sell-swords everywhere. Don't look like a bounty.
Everyone up here's hunting the Bugmaster or hunting someone like us.
Someone's already dead on that road.
Mercenaries gather here to prove a point. I'm too old to prove anything.
Whoever's out here with us is working. Don't turn your back.
Rim's a fine place to sell a rumour and a bad place to be one.
The inside of the ring is not for us.
Please don't go in. Please don't even look in.
Everyone is carrying a weapon. Why is everyone carrying a weapon?
I think I'm going to be sick. Is that allowed?
They said people who walk there never walk back.
A ring of mountains and one big bad idea inside.
Plenty of drifters out here, all sure they're the clever one.
Let's not be adventurers. Adventurers die with an embarrassing tale.
I like this edge. Edges are for turning around.
Many warriors come here to die gloriously. I'd prefer a better reason.
The Bugmaster isn't an enemy. He's a sentence passed on the foolish.
Hunters crawl this ring like ants at a corpse. They are not us.
We circle the mountain. We do not climb it.
Something dwells within the ring. We feel it as a missing note.
The hunters here smell of fear.
No one returns from the middle. We won't be the first.
The mountains hold. We hold each other.
Arach lies beyond the rim. Hazard level: extreme.
Bounty hunters present. Recommend minimal contact.
I recall instructions never to proceed past this point.
The route is a circle. I approve of circles.
Holy mines and nobody to run them. Starvers do the running now.
Big dust wall off there. Don't walk into that. Not for coin, not for love.
Bull herds out here. Never seen so much beef in one place and not a bite for us.
Empty roads, loud bellies. I know how this ends.
No patrols, and the hungry know it.
A dust wall in the south. Visibility is going to be nothing soon.
Starvers come in numbers. Keep your back on solid rock.
Abandoned mines are ideal camps and ideal graves.
It's so empty. And yet I feel like someone is counting us.
Are the bulls dangerous? They look very, very large.
I can see bones. Do I have to see bones?
The ground is so dry it hurts to breathe.
Good dust, bad company. Nothing new.
Empty land, hungry people. Keep your pockets quiet.
You could lose a god in this much nothing.
Bulls! Free steaks on the hoof. Never mind.
This land belongs to the Holy Nation, and they can't hold it. It makes them look like children.
Hungry men are the most dangerous.
I smell a sandstorm. Cover your face.
Starvers fight with empty bellies. I feel pity, but I won't slow.
The land is hungry. We're hungry.
We feel the wall of dust far away. It breathes.
No hive here. Only hunger.
People watch from the rocks. We don't wave.
Large dust wall detected. Visibility will degrade.
Holy mines abandoned. Material recovery possible.
Starving population hostile. Statistically unavoidable.
Central coordinates of the map confirmed.
Bones to the horizon. I used to think the stories were exaggerated.
Beak things and gorillo bandits. I miss quiet fights.
Dry, white, and bleached. Someone ate well here, once.
Mourn and Catun are around here somewhere.
Animals everywhere. You can't talk a beak thing out of anything.
Boneyard wolves hunt in packs. Don't run, they love it.
Watch your flanks. This ground makes ambushers of everything.
Fewer men than beasts. The beasts have the numbers.
It's all bones. Why is it all bones?
I stepped on a skull. A very recent skull.
Something is following us. It has long legs.
Are those teeth marks? Those are teeth marks.
Nothing living grows here. Nothing living wants to.
A land that eats its visitors.
Bones are good for one thing: remembering what not to do.
Keep your sword loose and your drink tight.
A hunting ground. We hunt here as equals with the beasts.
The wolves howl. Let them. We have answers.
Bones show who failed. Do not add to them.
The Empire's rot hasn't reached here. The animals keep it honest.
The old dead lie everywhere. We hear them, softly.
Beasts watch us. They don't fear us.
We move together or not at all.
Even the wind sings of something eaten.
Biological remains abundant. Fauna hostile.
Beak things detected. Fur deceptive. Teeth accurate.
Caution advised in tall grass. Wolf packs present.
I notice that the bones are the most common thing here.
No birds. No grass. Acid in the sky. This is how the world ends.
They tell me skeletons live out here.
Walk quick, keep your boots on, and don't drink the puddles.
Everything I own is going to rust.
Bring spare boots. The ground bites.
Iron spiders keep the roads. Stay off the roads.
The rain here will blister you. Find a roof and keep it.
One road in, same road out. I plan to use it.
It burns. The air burns.
My eyes are watering. Is that normal? Is that normal?
Please can we turn back? Please?
I can taste metal. I can taste rust.
Rust and rain. Our kind of holiday.
Keep your cloak up and your boots dry.
I've seen graveyards with better weather.
At least the dead don't ask for money.
This is a place for the machines. I'll leave it to them.
My skin tightens in this air. I'd like to leave it behind.
The acid isn't an honourable foe. It can't be fought.
Pass quickly. Don't linger. Don't ask the ground for anything.
The acid does not trouble us, but the silence does.
We aren't harmed here. We feel strange anyway.
Metal people live here. They watch from their windows.
Everything dead, everything quiet. We find we speak softer.
Home, in a manner of speaking. The rain doesn't harm me.
Iron spiders. Allied? Unclear. Neutral. Proceeding.
My companions will suffer here. Assistance recommended.
The Deadlands are not dead. They are waiting.
Black sand and black clouds. Mark my words, we're gonna cough.
Poison clouds drift here. Stay away from the dark ones.
I can't see the sun. I can't see a damn thing.
Whoever named this was being honest, at least.
Gas masks, or a handkerchief, or hold your breath. Pick fast.
Poison clouds move on the wind. Watch which way it blows.
Visibility low. Anything could be out here.
Keep the line tight and keep your face covered.
I can't breathe. I really can't breathe.
Why is the sand black? Is it supposed to be black?
I can feel my lungs hurting already.
Please get me out of here.
Cheerful place. A hundred ways to die and all of them cough.
Black sand. Might make a good dye.
Cover your face. Look dramatic doing it.
Never inhale deeply on a day like this. Every day is like this.
Dark clouds, dark sand. The Stone Golem would turn away.
I don't fear sand. I fear what clouds the lungs.
An honourable man dies in battle. Not like this.
Cover your mouth and hold your head high.
The poison doesn't like us either.
We move carefully. Each breath is a decision.
The dark sand drinks sound. Speak closer.
Together, together. Don't drift.
Toxic cloud density high. Organic personnel advised to mask.
I'm unaffected. They'll be affected.
Sand composition dark. Origin uncertain.
Fresh air isn't an option.
Swamp. Hemp, hashish and gangs. Good money, bad neighbours.
Visibility's rubbish. Anyone could be ten feet off.
Hounds run Shark. Don't ask who runs the rest.
I know three men who walked in here rich. I know none who walked out.
Gangs everywhere. Hounds, Stone Rats, Twinblades. Pick a path and don't bring the wrong colours.
Fog and foliage. Perfect for an ambush, perfect for a robbery.
Swamp raptors nest here. Don't step near the nests.
Every village a different crew. Nobody trusts a stranger with a sword.
It smells terrible. Everything is wet.
I can't see more than a few steps. What if they're right behind us?
Please don't touch the hemp. I don't want to know whose it is.
I'm sure there's a nice part. I'd like to find it.
Hemp, riceweed, and thieves. A drinker's heaven and a drinker's grave.
Smells like money and mildew. Pass the bottle.
Gangs love a fresh face. Don't be one.
Mud's soft on the feet. Hard on the pockets.
Swamp-dwellers fight like rats. We're better than rats.
Soft ground, soft men. Keep your spear sharp.
The fog hides cowards. Be what they aren't.
Squin guards the edge of this rot.
The air is thick and warm. Almost like the Hive.
Many small gangs, many small hungers. We shall not feed them.
We hear water, and boots in the water.
Plants grow here that dream. We don't drink from the pools.
Swamp terrain. Moisture ingress inevitable.
Gang territory. Multiple factions detected.
Visibility restricted. Radar not available.
Rust will accumulate. I'll accept the cost.
Big lake in the middle and a slave market on the east side. I stay out of that bit.
Swamp Ninjas and Red Sabres cutting at each other.
Everyone's selling something and half of it's people.
Stay off the east shore. Unless you want to be stock.
Sabres versus Ninjas. Never be between them.
A slave market. Don't linger where chains are visible.
Wet ground slows us. It slows them too, so be careful of that.
Keep the lake on one side and the ninjas on the other.
Slavers are here. I don't want to be anywhere with slavers.
Please, please don't let them see me.
The lake looks so calm. It isn't, is it?
Everyone around here has knives. Everyone.
Skirmishes in the reeds and markets on the shore. Lovely.
I know a man who sells his own cousins. He lives here.
Pretty lake. Pity about everything around it.
Smile for the slavers, boys. They don't tip.
Slavers trade in flesh. I'd make an end to them.
Swamp ninjas strike from reeds. A coward's craft.
Don't let them take any of us. I'll cut anyone who tries.
We won't stay here. The air offends me.
Many have been sold here. We hear their echoes.
Don't stay. The water remembers who cried into it.
We have seen the cages. We will not see them again.
Slavers don't value our song.
Slave market identified. Organic and inorganic personnel at risk.
Rival factions engaged in local conflict.
Wet terrain. Reduced mobility.
I've been sold before. I recall the experience.
Quiet for once. Caravans, a bit of shade. I could get used to it.
Safe enough that I'm suspicious.
Chad's somewhere around here. Fair warning, he will want to sell you something.
Somebody's selling robot limbs in the town. Don't ask what they cost.
Trade caravans and little else. A good place to take a breath.
Calm ground. Be ready for the day the calm breaks.
The travel shop's the thing here. Look, don't buy, unless you can afford the limbs.
Rest, then supply, then leave. I don't trust peace.
Oh. It's peaceful. It's so nice and peaceful.
Is it safe? Is it really safe here?
Look, a market. There might be bread.
I could stay here. I could stay here forever.
A lagoon! Shade, drink, and honest rogues.
Pull up a seat, friends. The world can wait an hour.
Caravans and gossip. Two things worth the walk.
No one's trying to kill us. I almost miss it.
A trading ground. I don't trust coin that flows so easily.
Peaceful lands make weak men. Keep your grip.
I shall observe the merchants. Perhaps even buy.
Rest, but do not sleep too deep.
The people here are calm. We find this unsettling.
Caravans pass without fear. We won't frighten them.
A rare quiet. We shall listen to it.
It's nice to hear no one scream.
Low threat environment. Resupply recommended.
Robotic limbs available for purchase. Interest noted.
Trade traffic high. Opportunity for exchange.
The lagoon is acceptable. Humidity less so.
Traders Guild country. Everything has a price including our hides.
Manhunters and slavers on every road. Walk like you're not worth the chains.
Canyon walls, convoys, and bribes. Keep some cats in your boot.
Heng. Where honest folk go broke and thieves go respectable.
Guild guards, slave convoys, bounty hunters. Count the badges before you stop.
Bribes first, questions later. That's how it works here.
Everyone is selling someone. Make sure it isn't us.
Patrols check wallets before weapons.
So many guards. So many chains.
I have a little money. I'd hate to lose it. I'd hate to lose more.
Please don't talk to anyone with a ledger.
This is the largest city I've seen. I wish it were smaller.
Heng. Pay your tolls, pay your drinks, pay your debts.
A city of gold and gutters.
Lots of money here. Lots of men who want it. Count your fingers after every handshake.
Smile, sign nothing, pay in small coin.
Coin-worshippers and chains. I don't like this place.
Don't let the merchants flatter you. They're valuing your blade.
The slavers watch us. Let them.
Many flatskins have sold their honour here. I won't.
Many are chained here. We're quiet.
The traders' laughter is hollow. We hear it echo.
Ledgers and chains, ledgers and chains.
We won't stay. We don't like what's counted here.
Heavy commercial traffic. Slave trading highly active.
Taxes and tolls likely. Funds recommended.
Bounty hunter presence confirmed. Avoid eye contact.
Many beings here are priced. I don't wish to know mine.
Blue sand, iron trees, beak things the size of horses. This is a bad place to be hungry.
Plenty of eggs out here, if you can steal them from the mothers.
Beak things eat people alive. Don't give them the chance.
Pretty colour, ugly neighbours.
Gutters and beak things. Don't fight them in the open.
Eggs and skins, profit and danger. Pick your share.
Strong skins sell well. Dying doesn't.
Dunes hide a lot. Watch the low points.
It's pretty. The sand is blue. Why is something so pretty so hungry?
Is that a beak thing? I know that it is. Please say it isn't.
I want to leave, quietly, right now.
Those trees look like iron. Why do they look like they're watching?
Blue sand. Pretty. Mind the teeth.
Eggs for dinner, if the owners don't object.
Hunters get rich here and die young. I'm already thinking about the first part.
Quiet, now. Let the big beaks sleep.
A good hunting ground. The beasts are worthy.
Beak things have no honour but they have appetite. I respect that.
Eggs and skins. We may trade well.
The sand is strange. Strange sand is a challenge.
The beaks are loud and hungry.
The trees sing a metal song. We don't know the words.
We tread softly. The sand will remember us.
Something big sleeps nearby. We don't wake it.
Beak thing population significant. Avoid nests.
Sand composition unusual. Possible mineral content.
Iron trees detected. Possible resource.
Fauna aggression high. Armour check recommended.
Dunes forever. United Cities cities poking up like thumbs.
Skimmers in the sand, starvers in the shade, slavers on the road.
Water. We should have brought more water.
Heft is somewhere ahead. Rich, loud, and full of guards.
Vagrants, manhunters, sand ninjas. The patrols here aren't friends.
Wide open dunes. No cover. Don't linger.
Slaver camps scattered through it. Don't wander near the fences.
Pay the toll. Walk on. Don't look at the cages.
It's so hot. And so empty. I don't think I like empty.
What are those moving shapes in the dunes? Are they skimmers?
I miss shade. I miss walls.
I can't see anyone. That doesn't mean no one is there.
Sand, gold, and trouble. An old combination.
Not a tree in sight. Good for drinking, bad for hiding.
Heft's wall is something to see. Don't be seen by it.
Pour one out for the traveller who forgot his water.
A desert like home but without the honour.
United Cities sprawl across it like fat in a stew.
Their patrols watch us. Let them pass.
Dunes are like seas. They carry the careless.
Many gather in the big cities. We can't hear them from here.
The sand sings loudly. We listen to it hum.
Skimmers move beneath the dunes. We feel them like a pulse.
We have little water. We shall be careful.
Desert heat noted. Component temperature rising.
Slave camps detected. Precaution recommended.
Skimmers present beneath the sand. Footfall caution.
United Cities territory. Documents unnecessary. Credits required.
Skimmers everywhere. The sand is crawling.
There's a prison round here with some very bad people in it.
Between the UC and the Holy Nation. Neither of them wants us, both of them are watching.
Sand ninjas hide near here. Hands on your purse.
Skimmers, mercenaries, escaped slaves. Everyone's on the run from someone.
Rebel farmers, too. Don't mistake them for bandits. Don't mistake them for friends.
Quiet ground and a prison close by.
Stay off the dune ridges. Skimmers love to ambush from a ridge.
Skimmers! They're everywhere!
A prison? Did you say a prison? Why would we be near a prison?
Please can we move on. Quietly.
I can hear them under the sand.
Sand, skimmers, and a jail. A fine neighbourhood for a nap.
Neutral ground, so I hear. Neutral ground has a nasty way of changing.
Keep a coin out for the next toll collector.
Never trust a quiet dune.
A buffer between flatskin nations. We belong to neither.
Skimmers are pests. Trample them.

Nobody wants to be here. Nobody lives here. There's a reason.
Two big nasties fighting each other.
Leave quick. We have no business.
Nests everywhere. Don't walk near them.
Beak things and crabs clash. Watch the edges of those fights.
Eggs sell well, if you survive to sell them.
Only enter if you have to. We have to.
Crabs! Beaks! Everything has claws!
I don't want the eggs. I just want out.
Can we run? Please?
Is that a nest? It's a nest.
Unwanted, huh? We fit right in.
Cheap eggs, expensive blood.
Crabs are tasty. Beak things less so.
Keep your hands away from the nests.
Beasts fighting beasts. Let them. We pass.
Eggs are good food. I wouldn't turn them down.
The zone earns its name.
Stay close to the edges.
Many small hearts beat in the nests.
Clicks and cries. They're afraid and angry.
We pass without troubling them.
Even the nests are lonely here.
Crab and beak thing population dense.
Eggs considered a resource. Retrieval hazardous.
Hostile fauna interacting. Avoid.
Don't stay. Don't hunt.
A city that used to be here. Now it's crabs and a few runaways.
Ruins in a maze. Easy to get lost, easy to get ambushed.
Land bridges under water. Walk where it's shallow.
Escaped slaves hide in the walls.
Crabs infest the lanes. Use doorways.
Escapees may be armed. Treat them cautiously.
Water on the bridges. Keep footing.
Old walls make perfect cover. For everyone.
It's a maze. We'll get lost.
I hear someone breathing behind that wall.
Were these people killed? The ruins are so empty.
Let's go back. I want to go back.
A maze with crabs. What a hobby.
Whoever built this had a sense of humour.
Walk where the ruins aren't. Walk where the crabs aren't.
Don't take that turn. Or do.
Walls that twist. A coward's city.
The slaves who hide here aren't our enemies.
Crabs are an honest foe. I'll fight them.
We keep to the straight path.
The walls hold old echoes. We listen.
Many fled here. We share their breath.
The maze is a puzzle. We solve it together.
We keep one hand on the wall.
Maze structure detected. Mapping initiated.
Crabs hostile. Escaped slaves unpredictable.
A city that vanished. I note it with sympathy.
Water covers the bridges. Avoid immersion.
Coast road. Easy way past the Hive, if you've got the nerve.
Fishmen and iron spiders along the beach.
It leads to the Ashlands, they say. I'd rather it led to a bar.
Cheaters run it because they're afraid. I'm afraid.
Shortcut to the Ashlands. Shortcuts cost.
Fishmen along the shore. Keep to the dunes.
Iron spiders patrol. Silence helps.
The Hive doesn't bother us here. Neither does anybody.
A run. Does that mean we have to run?
I hear splashing. Something is in the water.
Is it far to the Ashlands? I don't want to go there.
Please let this be quick.
Cheaters run, fools walk. We stroll.
Fishmen, spiders, a nice sea breeze. A holiday.
Nobody lives here, which suits me.
A shortcut to a dead land.
A route for those who avoid fights. I walk it with a heavy heart.
Fishmen are cowards of the water.
Spiders of iron. Cold, quiet, dangerous.
We pass quickly and say nothing.
We pass near the Southern Hive. We hear them faintly. We don't go in.
The sea sings in the distance.
Fishmen hunt here. They hunt with soft feet.
Be quiet, all of you.
Coastal route. Fishman and iron spider presence noted.
Shortcut to the Ashlands. Efficient.
Salt exposure low. Travel viable.
Route avoids Southern Hive. Diplomatic risk minimal.
A giant ring fell out of the sky and landed in the dust. I'd leave it.
Sandstorm all round it. Wind in your teeth.
Skimmers, bonedogs, bandits. Nobody here's sane.
Don't touch the ring. I'm serious.
Fallen satellite, central structure. Sandstorm cover.
Bandit groups roam. Keep close.
Visibility low. Maintain contact.
Whatever it was, it's still running.
What's that? It's so big.
The wind is so loud. I can't hear myself.
Is it still working? Is it watching?
I want to go home.
Big metal ring, loud wind, nowhere to hide. Like a bad wedding.
Sandstorm. Nature's own scrub.
Don't stare at it. It stares back.
A broken satellite. I've met worse.
A relic of the old world. It sleeps in the sand.
The wind tears at me. I welcome it.
Don't touch it. Don't stand near it.
It watches. I watch it back.
The ring hums. It's angry at itself.
We hear it in the dust.
Hold on to each other. The wind is strong.
Something old is trapped inside.
Fallen satellite detected. It's still running.
Another Eye operates in Venge. Related.
Sandstorm interference. Navigation degraded.
I know what it is. I won't explain.
Grey ground, grey sky, grey luck. One waystation and then nothing.
Nomads and smugglers. They'll sell you anything, including your own boots.
Oasis ahead, they say. Oases always have a thief at the water.
Nothing to rob here. Which means nothing to defend.
Sparse supplies. Fill every skin at the waystation.
Bloodraiders and smugglers. Keep to the high ground.
Polluted ground borders this land. Mind the wind.
A quiet stretch is the dangerous kind.
It's so grey. Everything is grey.
Please, is there water? Real water?
I feel like we're the only ones alive.
Who would live out here?
Grey, grey, grey. Let's stop and add some colour with a drink.
An oasis would do nicely. A mirage will do for now.
Smugglers know the best vintages. Just a thought.
Pretty empty. Prettier with a cup.
Sand and silence. I feel at home.
Nomads know the old ways. I'll listen.
Don't trust the smuggler's smile.
We rest at the oasis, if there's one.
The land is thin and quiet.
A few travel here, and they're wary. So are we.
We carry water for each other.
I like it quiet.
Resupply point: one waystation. Plan accordingly.
Pollution detected at the borders. Organic exposure risk.
Smugglers and nomads present. Contact optional.
The land is sparse. So is my interest.
UC frontier, and nothing past it but trouble. Grass pirates, crabs, beak things.
Crab Raiders hold the beach. Best leave them to it.
Wet, windy, wild. And every wave looks like a grin.
Pirates in the long grass. I never trust long grass.
Last UC outpost before the wild. Buy what you need now.
Crab Raiders and Reavers scrap on the sands.
Wind and rain. Crabs on the beach. Count on nothing.
Pirates strike from cover. Watch the grass.
It's so windy. It feels like the sea wants us.
Crabs! So many crabs.
Are pirates here? Real pirates?
I'd like to go home. Wherever that is.
Salt air and sharp claws. A bracing walk.
Grass pirates! I'd love to meet one. I'd love more to avoid one.
Last stop before the wild. Order double.
Stormy coasts are the best for secrets.
The sea is no friend of a desert man.
Crab raiders wear their shells with pride. I'll break them.
Pirates fight like thieves. We shall answer.
Keep dry, keep close.
The waves sing a lonely song.
Crabs click in the shallows. They don't like us.
The frontier is thin. We walk it carefully.
We shall not stay.
Coastal frontier. Salt corrosion probable.
Crab Raiders present in strength.
Pirate activity in the grass. Evasion recommended.
UC jurisdiction ends here. Safety does too.
Purple sand. Purple! And half-buried satellites. Somebody was here before us.
Iron spiders along the trail, some dead, some pretending.
Shriekers and cannibals wander in from the forests.
Glass underfoot. Walk soft.
Barren and sparse. Easy to spot enemies, easy to be spotted.
Spiders line the trail. Dead or alive, don't test them.
Cannibals and shriekers drift here from the west.
Old structures in the sand. Don't enter.
Why is the sand purple? Is it safe?
Those things in the sand look like eyes.
I don't want to step on the glass.
It's like walking on a dream I can't wake from.
Purple sand! Like a dye bath for the whole planet.
Glass floor, spider fences. A classy trail.
Skip the satellites. They've got stories I don't want.
Quiet. Pretty. Suspicious.
The sand has a strange colour. The Stone Golem would be curious.
Metal spiders on a glass road.
We keep to the trail and say nothing.
Cannibals roam here. Keep your spear near.
The sand hums a faint, strange note.
The spiders sleep. We hope they stay asleep.
The trail is thin. We follow in single file.
We hear the wind more than anything.
Unusual sand composition. Origin: unknown.
Iron spider fragments abundant. Active units possible.
Buried satellites detected. Don't disturb.
Glass ground reduces traction. Advise caution.
Sniperbots up in the rocks. I can't see them.
Don't run in straight lines. Don't stand still either.
Leviathans may turn up near the coast. Everything here wants us dead.
I feel eyes on the back of my head.
Sniperbots hold the heights. Use cover, move in bounds.
Avoid open ground. Keep to the shadows.
Cover each other. Talk in whispers.
No one stops. No one talks.
I feel something watching us. Something not alive.
Please, can we hurry? Please?
Don't make any noise.
I don't like this place at all.
A valley full of unseen snipers. Wonderful. Keep drinking, keep moving.
Sneak, don't strut. Even I know that.
Nothing like a little danger to sharpen the nerves.
Stay low. Stay lucky.
A coward's valley. Enemies who strike from afar.
I'd fight them face to face. They won't allow it.
We move swiftly, from rock to rock.
No honour in this ground.
The valley is watching. We feel it.
Machines up in the rock. They don't sing.
Quiet, all of us.
Together, together.
Sniperbot activity probable.
Cover density insufficient. Move.
I have a lower profile than you. I'll scout.
I recognise the units. They don't recognise me.
Ruins at the edge of the world. Not much to steal that someone else didn't.
Nobody lives here. Nobody remembers it.
Think of the stuff lying around. Then think of why it's still lying around.
End of the map. End of the road.
Old ruins everywhere. Scavenge, don't settle.
Abandoned ground. Abandoned for good reason.
Don't split up. Don't lose sight of the others.
We take what's useful and go.
It's so empty. Everything is empty.
Who left all this?
I don't want to touch anything.
Please let's not stay.
Ruins at the end of the world. I've been in worse bars.
Whoever lived here had good taste.
Pick through, pocket, and out.
I could retire here. I won't.
A land abandoned. A people forgotten.
These ruins held a proud people once, perhaps.
I'll take only what I need.
Move on.
The ruins whisper. They're kind whispers.
Nobody sings here. The silence is old.
We walk gently.
We leave things as they are.
Abandoned settlement. Salvage possible.
Resource density low. Proceed.
Ancient locations present. Hazard unknown.
A place the world forgot. I understand.
Bloodraiders and sand ninjas call this ridge home.
Rocky plateau, narrow passes. A bad road for a big group.
I hate canyons. You can't run sideways.
If a stone moves, it's probably a ninja.
Narrow passes. Don't bunch up. Rotate scouts.
Sand ninjas strike from the rock. Look for the shine.
Bloodraiders are loud. Ninjas aren't. Listen for the quiet.
High walls on both sides. Keep moving.
That shadow moved. I swear it moved.
It's so narrow. What if we get trapped?
Please, can we find another road?
I want sun and open sky.
Spine Canyon. Sounds like a bad back and feels like one.
Ninjas! Always ninjas. I'm sure they're lovely.
Quiet, now. If I smell blood, I'll offer a drink.
Pretty rock. Ugly company.
A canyon is a trap for the careless. We are careful.
Sand ninjas hide in shame. Let them.
Bloodraiders are fools. Their screams will draw them.
We hold the middle of the pass.
The walls are watching. We feel their eyes.
Many hearts beat in the stone.
We walk close together.
No song. No sound.
Canyon terrain. Ambush probability high.
Sand ninjas detected nearby. Silent. Dangerous.
Bloodraiders loud. Easy to avoid.
Narrow path. Single file recommended.
Rock squares in a grid. Looks like somebody ploughed the world with a ruler.
There's a workshop in here with good loot. And good guards, I'd wager.
Spikes, ridges, rows. A maze for the lazy.
Whoever built this had patience and no taste.
The grid layout channels movement. Predictable.
Workshops hold weapons and research. Expect defenders.
Stay off the ridges. Stay low.
Follow the rows. Don't cross them.
It looks so strange. Like a game board.
Are we the pieces? I don't like that thought.
Everything is so straight.
Where's the way out?
A world-sized chessboard. Pretty, in a deadly sort of way.
Workshops mean loot. Loot means drinks.
Don't take a wrong turn. Or do.
I wonder who played here.
An odd land, laid out by a stranger's hand.
The rows are straight. Straight is honest.
A workshop of the old ones.
Walk the lines. Do not wander.
The ground has a pattern. We find it calming.
Old minds laid this out. We hear their echo.
We follow the rows together.
Quiet. The ridges listen.
Grid pattern consistent with agricultural design.
Workshop complex ahead. Research possible.
Famine event logged in archives. Cause uncertain.
I don't know who planned this.
Still breathing. Pity about the face.
Who hit me? Never mind. Where's my stuff?
Ugh. Count the heads. Count my teeth.
Still here. Still ugly. Still owed money.
Down and back up. Report: nothing broken that matters.
How long was I out? Anybody take anything?
Fine. I'm fine. Give me a minute.
Over, then. Good. Check the others.
Is it over? Is it really over? Am I dead?
Oh. Oh no. I fainted again, didn't I?
I'm alive. I'm alive and that's all I ask.
Please tell me everyone is here.
Mm. Head like a drum. Anyone have a drink?
Alive. That's the first good news of the day.
Not my best landing. Where did the sky go?
I dreamt of a warm bar. Now this.
I yielded to sleep. A lesser enemy would not have done it.
I fell. I rise. That is the whole of a warrior.
Is the fight finished? Did I miss glory?
My body fails sooner than my will.
We are awake. We are still ours.
The song returns slowly. We're here.
We were away. Are we all present?
Our head hums. We shall endure.
Systems restored. Damage assessment initiated.
Offline for an interval. Resuming.
Self-check complete. Proceed.
Function resumed. Report accepted.
Beep.
Beep? Beep beep.
Beep... beep.
Beep beep beep.
Hungry and beaten. Great combination.
I need to eat. I need to eat before I hit anyone.
Fainted twice and ate nothing. Fix that first.
Somebody feed me. Anything. I'll work it off.
Down on an empty stomach. Careless. Feed me before the next one.
Hunger makes me slow. I'll note that for later.
We eat first. Everything else second.
A fighter who doesn't eat is a body waiting.
I'm so hungry. I fell down because I'm so hungry.
I need bread. Please, any bread.
Is there food? Tell me there's food.
My stomach is eating itself.
Feed me or finish me. I'll accept either, in that order.
Hungry, bruised, and sober. A new low.
I was mid-dream about a roast. Don't speak of it.
If anyone has crumbs, I'll sell my boots for them.
I will not complain. My belly will.
Food. A warrior eats, then fights.
I fall hungry and rise hungry. I'll endure.
We must find meat. Soon.
We're hungry. We're all hungry.
The hum in our head is our hunger.
Without food we forget the song.
We shall not complain. But we're faint.
Organic personnel advised to eat. Immediately.
Nutrition critical for the others. I note it.
My needs are different. Yours are urgent.
Recommend food acquisition. Priority high.
Beep. Beeeep.
Beep? Beep beep... beep.
Beep. Beep. Beep.
Beep beep.
My leg. Somebody splint my leg.
Can't walk right. Somebody carry my stuff.
Hurts like hell. It's broken, isn't it?
Leg's gone. Don't leave me behind.
Leg's broken. Splint it. Then we move.
I'll limp. I'll slow you down.
Bone's gone. I need a splint kit.
Don't make me crawl. Don't leave me.
My leg! It hurts so much!
I can't walk. I can't. Please help.
Please don't leave me here. Please.
It's bent in a way it shouldn't.
My leg's folding the wrong way. Pass the bottle.
I've had better days. And better legs.
Don't laugh. It hurts when I laugh.
Splint. Drink. In that order.
A broken leg is a warrior's reminder.
I'll walk again. I'll walk faster.
Don't carry me. Let me hobble.
Bone mends. Honour doesn't.
Our leg is hurt. It hums with pain.
We can't walk well. Please carry us a little.
We feel our bone sing wrong.
We slow. We apologise.
Limb damage detected. Replacement recommended.
Mobility degraded. Splint required.
Movement slowed. Plan adjustments needed.
I'll repair. Give me time.
Beep! Beep beep!
Beep... beep...
Beep beeeep.
Beep? Beep.
Arm's busted. Can't swing a thing.
Give me my sword in the other hand. Not that hand.
Arm hurts like a bastard.
Great. Now I'm useless.
Arm is broken. I can still carry.
Splint. Quickly. Please.
I'll cover your backs. I can't use my arm.
Keep it still. Don't tell me to relax.
My arm! It's wrong, it's wrong!
It hurts so much. Please do something.
I can't lift anything now. Not even my bag.
Please don't make me hold anything.
Well, there goes my drinking arm. The other one will have to learn.
Arm's broken. Mood's fine. Odd.
Someone find me a stick.
Don't touch it. I'll scream.
A broken arm is not a broken will.
I'll fight with the other.
Bind it. We move.
I have suffered worse.
Our arm hangs wrong. Please bind it.
We hold it close. We hum around the hurt.
We can't lift. We apologise.
We're weaker for now.
Arm damage detected. Function reduced.
Capability: 50 percent. Request support.
Splint or replacement advised.
I'll adapt.
Beep! Beep!
Beep beep... beep.
Beeeeep.
Beep? Beep.
My skull's ringing like a bell. Say something quiet.
Head's cracked. Don't hit it again.
Everything's spinning. Don't ask me names.
Think I got hit with a brick. Or a hammer.
Head took a beating. Give me a moment to see straight.
Concussion. Don't let me lead.
Fogged. Not dead. Not fit either.
Skull's sore. I'll live.
My head... why is the room moving?
I can't think. I can't remember. Who are you?
Please tell me I haven't lost any memory.
It hurts. It hurts so much.
Oh, my head. Not a drop of drink involved.
Skull's complaining. I'm ignoring it.
I see stars. Pretty ones.
Ask me tomorrow what my name is.
My skull is stone. It cracked, but it holds.
A blow to the head. A gift. I'll return it.
Don't speak loudly.
I remember everything. Mostly.
Our head hums wrong. The song is broken.
We can't hear the others properly.
We're confused. Please be patient.
Our thoughts fall apart.
Cranial damage. Cognitive function degraded.
Memory banks inconsistent. Stand by.
Running diagnostics. Please wait.
Head assembly compromised.
Beep... beeeeep.
Beep? Beep? Beep?
Beep beep beep.
Bzzzzz. Beep.
Next time I hit first. Next time I hit harder.
That all they had? I'm still standing.
Anyone else want a go? I'm ready.
I've been hit by worse. Mostly sober.
I'll learn from that. And I'll win the next one.
Good fight. I was unlucky. Not beaten.
Get me a drink and get me my sword.
I'm back. Let's finish this.
Round two, anyone? I'll buy.
Death will have to try harder.
Ah, that's better. Where's my hat?
I fell asleep. Wake me for the fun.
I fell, and I rose. That's courage.
Next time, they'll fall.
I don't fear pain. I fear dishonour.
I'm ready.
We aren't afraid.
We endure for the Hive. We endure.
We fell. We rise.
We won't be broken.
Combat readiness restored.
I'll resume engagement.
Fear isn't part of my configuration.
Damage minor. Proceeding.
I'm alive? I'm alive. Don't let me do that again.
Never again. Never. Never.
Is it over? Is anyone still out there?
I thought that was the end. I really did.
I don't like this. I don't like it. We should leave.
Close one. Too close.
Be honest, how bad was it?
Somebody keep watch. Please.
I'm so scared. I'm so scared.
Please don't leave me alone.
I thought I died.
I'm never fighting anyone again.
Terrifying. Passes for entertainment, I suppose.
I'm going to need several drinks.
Who stole my courage?
That's it. I'm retiring.
I... was afraid. I won't speak of it.
I'll conquer this fear.
Don't tell the others.
I live. That's enough.
We're afraid. We're afraid.
We hear the fear. It's ours.
Please stay close. Please.
We're small.
Preservation instinct noted.
Fear is irrational. It remains.
Recommend withdrawal.
My composure is reduced.
Not done yet. Not by a long shot.
You hit like a mule. Do it again.
Back up. Back up and bleeding.
Up! Up and angry!
Back on my feet. Cover me.
Not out yet. Not today.
Still in it. Keep them off me.
Up. Weapon ready. Go.
I'm up! I'm up! Don't leave me!
Please don't hit me again.
Oh no. They're still fighting.
I'll... I'll try. I'll try.
Round two! Hand me my sword.
Wasn't dead, just resting.
Is it my turn? It's my turn.
I got up. Somebody applaud.
I rise! For honour!
I won't stay down while others fight.
Blood and sand. I stand.
Kral's name, I live yet.
We rise. We fight for the others.
We aren't finished. We aren't.
The Hive doesn't fall.
We get up. We always get up.
Systems online. Re-engaging.
Combat function restored.
Rising. Weapons ready.
Ready. Targets acquired.
Beep! Beep beep!
Beep beeeep!
Beep!
Beep beep beep beep!
More of them than us. Great.
Up and still losing. Ha.
Count: lots. Us: not lots. Brilliant.
If we die, I'm blaming whoever picked this fight.
Outnumbered. Fall back and form a line.
Odds are bad. Pick your targets.
Don't die stupid. Die expensive.
Hold the line. We do the maths later.
There are so many of them!
We're going to die. We're all going to die.
Please let someone have a plan.
Can we not fight them? Can't we run?
Outnumbered! It's fine. I've been outnumbered at every bar I've ever drunk in.
Eight of them, four of us.
We can win this. In a very imaginative way.
Don't count them. It only makes things worse.
Many against few. The Stone Golem sees us.
Glory is cheapest when the odds are worst.
Let them come. We choose the ground.
Strength isn't in numbers.
Many against us. We are many too, in song.
Stand together. Together we are larger.
We don't run. We never run.
The Hive endures.
Odds unfavourable. Withdrawal advised.
Numerical disadvantage confirmed.
Formation tight. Pick off the nearest.
Survival probability low. Continuing anyway.
I'll fight when I'm fed. Not before. But I'll fight.
Hunger makes me mean. Good.
Empty stomach, full temper.
Up. Hungry. Angry. Dangerous.
No food in me and a fight on. Careless.
Hunger is a weapon. So is spite.
Quick and clean. I can't afford long.
Nobody tell me I look weak.
I'm starving. I'm starving and they're attacking.
Why do we always fight on an empty belly?
I feel faint. I feel faint again.
Please finish this soon.
Fighting hungry. A romantic notion.
Just kill them before they take my appetite.
Hungry, injured, undefeated. Pass the sword.
I want a roast. They'll do.
Hunger is a lesson. I learn.
A starved warrior is the most dangerous.
I rise empty. I fight full.
I have endured worse.
We are hungry. We fight anyway.
Fighting without food is hard. We try.
We're tired. We're here.
We endure the hunger.
Organic reserves low. Combat efficiency reduced.
Continuing engagement. Hunger noted.
Protect organics. Prioritise feeding after combat.
Rising.
Wasn't even a fair hit. Guess I'm a sleeper.
Fell for nothing. Then someone's lucky.
That wasn't even a fight, was it? Embarrassing.
Don't tell anyone I went down for that.
Down for no reason. I'll fix that habit.
Careless. I'll watch my footing.
Wasted time. Up and moving.
My fault. It won't happen twice.
I fell over. Again.
Did anyone see that? Please say no.
I'm clumsy. I'm so clumsy.
I'm sorry for the trouble.
Dropped for a nap. Resumed.
I blame the drink. And the ground.
Must've tripped over a god's toe.
Well, that was undignified.
I fell without an enemy. A bitter taste.
That wasn't a defeat. That was a misstep.
I'll remember this and not repeat.
Say nothing.
We fell, for no good reason.
We're all right. We're all right.
We apologise for the delay.
Please don't tell the others.
Unexpected shutdown. Cause under review.
Balance sensors compromised.
Resume operation.
Fall unnecessary. Recorded.
Beep.
Beep beep.
Beep? Beep.
Beep beep beep.

say: Down you stay. I'll have them boots.
Just me, then, and it was enough.
Shame nobody was here to see that.
Right. Pockets.
Clear. One left standing, and it's me.
Done. Patch up, move on.
Still here, on my own. That'll have to do.
Contact over. Keep walking.
I did that? I did that on my own.
Is anyone there? No. Just me, then.
My hands won't stop shaking. It's over, though.
I won. Nobody's going to believe it.
Unbeaten, unwatched, and dreadfully thirsty.
A pity there's no one to tell. I'll tell them later, at length.
Another one for the story. I'll improve it in the telling.
Stay down. I've a drink to find.
One against many. The Stone Golem would approve.
No witnesses. The honour counts all the same.
Rise if you can. No? Then it is done.
I stood alone, and I still stand.
Done. No hive to tell. Only me.
I won. Nobody cheers. I did not expect them to.
It is over. I am one, and that is enough.
No one to hear it. I say it anyway: I won.
Hostiles neutralised. No allies in range. Logging it anyway.
Engagement concluded. Sole unit operational.
Threat removed. Proceeding alone.
All clear. Unit intact.
Beep. Beep!
Beep...
Beep beep beep!
Beep!
Down they go. Take their boots.
That's that. Check the pockets.
Not so tough. Not so rich either.
Done. Anyone bleeding who shouldn't be?
Clear. Count heads. Check wounds.
Contact ended. Reload, regroup, move.
Done. Don't linger.
That was clean. Remember it.
Is it over? It's over. We won?
I didn't even hit anyone. Did anyone?
Oh, thank goodness. Thank goodness.
I'm shaking. Are they dead?
There. A fine day's work, and the day's barely begun.
Pour one for the fallen. Mostly for me.
